paper_sections.title: Promoter haplotypes of interleukin-10 gene linked to cortex plasticity in subjects with risk of Alzheimer's disease
2.8 Statistical analysis involving demographic and neuropsychological data

description.value: The study examined whether IL-10 promoter ATA haplotype status is associated with hippocampal functional connectivity and its relationship to cognition in amnestic mild cognitive impairment and healthy older adults.

design.value: A cross-sectional resting-state functional MRI study recruited 39 aMCI subjects and 30 healthy controls, genotyped them for three IL-10 promoter polymorphisms, and compared bilateral hippocampal networks using a two-way groups-by-haplotypes ANOVA followed by post-hoc group comparisons and correlations with neuropsychological scores.

description.value: The first eight volumes were discarded to allow for T1 equilibration effects. Remaining images were corrected for timing differences and motion effects, spatially normalized into the SPM5 Montreal Neurological Institute echo-planar imaging template with resampling to 3 × 3 × 3 mm3 voxels, and smoothed with an 8 × 8 × 8 mm3 Gaussian kernel. REST software was then used to remove the linear trend of time courses and apply temporal bandpass filtering at 0.01–0.08 Hz.

steps.value: The first eight volumes of the scanning session were discarded to allow for T1 equilibration effects.
The remaining images were corrected for timing differences and motion effects.
Participants with head motion of > 3 mm maximum displacement along any axis, or 3° of any type of angular motion were excluded.
The resulting images were spatially normalized into the SPM5 Montreal Neurological Institute echo-planar imaging template using default settings and resampling to 3 × 3 × 3 mm3 voxels.
The normalized images were smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 8 × 8 × 8 mm3.
REST software was used to remove the linear trend of time courses.
REST software was used for temporal bandpass filtering (0.01–0.08 Hz).

model_settings.value: The bilateral hippocampus was set as the ROI using automated anatomic labelling implemented with wfu_Pick-Atlas software. For each subject, a mean ROI time series was computed, cross-correlation was carried out between the mean ROI signal change and every voxel time series, and a Fisher's z-transform was applied to the correlation coefficients. Six head motion parameters and the mean time series of global, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals were introduced as covariates. Voxelwise-based grey matter volume correction was also applied.

estimator.value: cross-correlation analysis followed by Fisher's z-transform

model_settings.value: ANOVA: groups × haplotypes; groups: aMCI and controls; haplotypes: without ATA haplotype and with ATA haplotype. Statistical thresholds were set at corrected p < 0.05 by Monte Carlo simulation for multiple comparisons, with single voxel p value = 0.05, minimum cluster size = 10,503 mm3, FWHM = 8 mm, with mask.
The mean value of functional connectivity within the mask of ANOVA interactions was extracted from each subject's image and used for further group comparisons.
Correlation between neuropsychological test scores and the mean value of functional connectivity within the mask of ANOVA interactions.
